performance-memory.summary: Know how V8 turns JavaScript into fast machine code, what makes it slow down again, and how to find and fix memory leaks with real measurements instead of folklore.
points: V8 tiers code from the Ignition interpreter to the Sparkplug, Maglev and TurboFan compilers, using type feedback. Deoptimization falls back to the interpreter when assumptions break.
Hidden classes (shapes) depend on property order. Create objects in one place with every field initialised, and avoid `delete` in hot paths so inline caches stay monomorphic.
Arrays track elements kinds (SMI → DOUBLE → ELEMENTS, packed or holey), and transitions are one-way. Avoid holes and mixed types in hot arrays.
GC is generational: a cheap scavenger handles the young generation, and concurrent mark-compact handles the old. Allocation rate drives GC frequency.
Leaks are unintended references: uncleared timers and listeners, detached DOM nodes, unbounded caches, closures sharing a context. Use the three-snapshot technique and the retainers view.
Watch for Big-O traps: `includes` inside loops (use a Set), `shift` queues, and spreading inside `reduce`. Move CPU-bound work to workers, and transfer buffers instead of copying them.
traps: A microbenchmark whose result is never used may be measuring nothing at all, because of dead-code elimination.
`FinalizationRegistry` callbacks may never run. Never rely on them to release resources.
`heapUsed` doesn't include Buffer contents, and `--max-old-space-size` doesn't limit off-heap memory.
